metadata.datasource:
Prepared for Negs from the manufacturer's brochure: FUJICOLOR POSITIVE FILM ETERNA-CP 3512/3612 brochure, Ref. No. KB-1002E, (c) 2010 FUJIFILM Corporation, PDF page 1 (spectral sensitivity, per-dye spectral density, characteristic curves). PDF sha256 5236a371b0a211ca0a99876b14c3f06bb76d34820a5e15839001db25c581192e. Data (c) FUJIFILM Corporation. The curves were read from the PDF's vector paths (tools/film_profiles/extract_pdf.py); the points and axis calibration are in data/profile-sources/fujifilm-print/fujifilm_eterna_cp_3512/.
Method: spektrafilm's public-era profile creator by Andrea Volpato (commit b2c7fe6), its steps for papers and print films: D-min removed (base synthesised from the curves' D-min), log E zero where green is 0.735 over D-min, Fujifilm's own per-dye spectra scaled so equal amounts view as an 18.4 % neutral under the viewing illuminant (K75P), status-A unmixing, a 3 norm_cdfs curve fit, densitometer normalisation. Then the author's print normalisation (spektrafilm #557): sensitivities scaled so the TH-KG3 enlarger lamp through Y50 M50 and the mid-scale neutral of kodak_vision3_250d gives raw exposure 1 per channel. Negs step before the unmixing: each status-A curve moved along log E so log E 0 develops the metameric neutral's status-A density (the private creator's preliminary neutral shift; R +0.214, G -0.013, B +0.062 log E). Calibration: the same steps rebuild Kodak 2383 and 2393 from spektrafilm's public raw data to within CIEDE2000 0.9-1.0 mean (2.6 at most) of the shipped profiles on a ColorChecker printed from cine negatives, and their neutral filters within about 3 CC (data/profile-sources/fujifilm-print/calibration/). Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md D12.
Brochure specifics: the characteristic curves' log H axis is unlabelled (one square is 0.5 log H), and green and blue are plotted 1.0 and 2.0 log H to the left of red; the shift is undone, and the pre-alignment fixes each channel's position anyway. Fujifilm draws each dye curve with the film base under it (where all four are drawn, Y + M + C - Gray = 2 x base). The base taken off is the one fujifilm_eterna_cp_3513di's dye chart implies (this brochure shares one hand-drafted dye chart with three others, whose Gray disagrees with its dyes by up to 0.1 D, so it cannot give its own; the same film base is assumed), smoothed 20 nm. Undrawn parts filled: cyan 400-485 nm from fujifilm_eterna_cp_3513di's net dye, scaled 0.919 to this dye over their overlap and joined at the drawn end (step +0.044 D tapered off over 30 nm); magenta 650-695 nm from fujifilm_eterna_cp_3513di's net dye, scaled 0.944 to this dye over their overlap and joined at the drawn end (step -0.009 D tapered off over 30 nm). Sensitivity is drawn only near each peak (red in two pieces, 391-433 nm and 645-715 nm): beyond each drawn end it continues with the shape of kodak_2383 (Kodak's ECP-2 print film, the calibration stock), joined at the end and only falling away from it. Share of the normalisation's raw exposure from these tails: R 25%, G 1%, B 0% (red: mostly 600-640 nm, where an orange-masked negative passes the most light).
Checks: curve fit within 0.029 D; status-A remix within 0.029 D of the brochure's curves up to D 2.0 and 0.068 D above; raw exposure 1 per channel through the reference film.
Negs choices: reference illuminant TH-KG3 and viewing illuminant K75P, use 'cine' and antihalation 'strong', as the shipped spektrafilm Kodak 2383; log_sensitivity_density_over_min 1.0 as printed (reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) for density 1.0 above minimum density); spectra left empty (null) outside 400-695 nm for the dyes; characteristic curves in log10 H. Printed as 2854K tungsten, 1/100 s, Fuji SC-41 + CC-90Y + CC-60M; ECP-2B.
Recorded exceptions: characteristic x axis, gate 0.4 % of span: Hand-drafted grid: the 12 log H gridlines are spaced 17.3-19.4 pt for one 0.5 log H square, so no straight line meets all of them; the worst is 0.38 % of span (0.02 log H). The neutral pre-alignment fixes each channel's position, so only the slope matters, and it is the mean square. characteristic x axis (relative): Exposure [log H] carries no numbers, only a 0.5 log H scale bar spanning one grid square; the offset is arbitrary (log E 0 is set by step 2 and the neutral pre-alignment) and the scale is 0.5 log H per square. characteristic y axis, gate 0.4 % of span: Hand-drafted grid: the density gridlines are spaced 18.0-19.1 pt for 0.5 D; the worst is 0.33 % of span (0.015 D). Checked against the drawn D-max of the companion brochure (3512/3514DI/3523XD share the template). spectral_density x axis, gate 0.7 % of span: Hand-drafted grid shared by four brochures (3521XD, 3512, 3514DI, 3523XD): the 400/500/600/700 nm gridlines are 50.4, 47.5 and 48.7 pt apart; the worst is 0.63 % of span (2 nm). Physical check: the dye peaks fall within 3 nm of 3513DI's precisely drawn chart (D12). sensitivity y axis (relative): Relative spectral sensitivity (log): each channel's level is renormalised (D12 step 7), so only the scale matters; it is set by the two labelled gridlines (2.0, 1.0). curve fit, gate 0.03: the brochure's blue curve is straight and steep from D 1 to about 2.8 and then turns into its shoulder within about 0.1 log H; three norm_cdfs per channel cannot follow both, so blue misses by up to 0.029 D around D 1-2.3 (red and green within 0.017 D). Upstream fits with the same model.
